data.gender_notes: Pet is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'petra' meaning rock or stone. In Christian tradition, the name Pet is a derivative of Peter, which means 'rock' or 'stone' in Greek. This name holds significant meaning as a symbol of faith and strength. The name Pet carries the meaning “Rock, Stone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Pet usually hope their child will grow to embody rock, stone and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of steadfast faith and strength
data.etymology: Pet belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rock, Stone.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pet total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_greek.name: Πέτρος
in_greek.long_meaning: a transliteration of the Hebrew name Petach or Petah, meaning 'rock' in Greek, as in the name of the disciple Peter

in_latin.name: Petrus
in_latin.long_meaning: a Latinized form of the Greek name Petros, meaning 'rock'

in_english.name: Pet
in_english.long_meaning: derived from the Old English word pēt, meaning 'stone, pebble, or rock', or from the Greek name Petros, meaning 'rock'

data.cultural_impact: Pet was a common name among early Christians, particularly in reference to Saint Peter, one of the twelve apostles and the first Pope. The name Pet or Pete represents a strong and steadfast individual, much like the rock on which Jesus built his Church (Matthew 16:18). It has been passed down through generations and remains a popular name in various Christian communities today.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Pet is a constant reminder of the faith and steadfastness that Saint Peter demonstrated throughout the New Testament. The name carries the spiritual weight of loyalty and resilience, inspiring those who bear it to embody these virtues in their own lives. It also symbolizes the foundation of one's faith, resembling a rock upon which all belief is built.
